```markdown
<the fact; for feedback/project, follow with **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].>
```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

 - Fast mode for Claude Code uses Claude Opus with faster output (it does not downgrade to a smaller model). It can be toggled with /fast.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

17	
18	多分类交叉熵衡量预测分布与真实分布的差异。对单个样本，设预测 logits 经 softmax 得到概率 \( p = (p_0, p_1, \dots, p_{C-1}) \)，真实类别为 \( y \)，则：

22	\]

76	= \left[
77	\underbrace{I_1,\dots,I_K}_{\text{base 实例行}}\ ;\ 
78	\underbrace{P_1,\dots,P_M}_{\text{SAM3D 伪掩码行}}\ ;\ 
79	\underbrace{C_0,C_1,\dots,C_{19},U}_{\text{语义 one-hot 行（末行 } U \text{ 为 unlabeled 兜底）}}

81	\]

201	### 4.2 模块二：`query_masks`——查询采样后的 GT 同步裁剪
202	
203	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
204	
205	`sp_masks` 的列坐标是「场景内全部超点」。但 u4-l1 讲过：训练前向里 `_select_queries` 会按 `query_thr=0.5` 随机丢弃一部分超点查询（省算力 + 增广效果），只有存活查询才进入解码器。于是产生一个对齐问题：**预测 `sem_preds`/`masks` 的第 j 列对应的是「存活查询 j」，而 GT 的第 c 列对应的是「超点 c」——两套列坐标不一致了**。
206	
207	解法：采样时把被选中的超点下标 `ids` 记下来，用 `sp_masks[:, ids]` 把 GT 的列同步裁剪到存活查询上，结果存成 `query_masks`。所以：
208	
209	- `sp_masks` = 完整视图：行 = GT 条目，列 = **全部超点**；
210	- `query_masks` = 训练视图：行 = GT 条目（**行不变**），列 = **存活的查询**。
211	
212	`query_masks` 在总调度里被切片后随各路 GT 一起传给子损失；匹配器（u5-l2）据此只在存活查询上做匹配，损失计算也在存活列上进行——被丢弃的查询从训练中完全消失，等价于「这个超点今天不参与监督」。
213	
214	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
215	
216	```text
217	_select_queries（每个场景）：
218	    若 query_thr < 1：
219	        n ∼ Uniform(query_thr, 1) × 超点数，再截断到 ≤ 3500
220	        ids = 随机排列取前 n 个            # 存活超点的原始下标
221	        queries = 超点特征[ids]            # 预测侧：只保留这些查询
222	        query_masks = sp_masks[:, ids]     # GT 侧：列同步裁剪
223	    否则：
224	        queries = 全部超点特征
225	        query_masks = sp_masks             # 退化为完整视图
226	```
227	
228	随后在总调度里：`sem_gt` 优先用 `query_masks[-n-1:, :]`，`inst_gt` 附带 `query_masks[:-n-1, :]`（见 4.1.3）；提示 GT 的 `query_masks` 原样透传（提示查询是从特定超点生成的，天然在存活集合内，无需再裁）。

279	### 4.3 模块三：五个子损失的调用顺序与 loss 字典合并
280	
281	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
282	
283	拆分完 GT，总调度开始「发货」。五个子损失的调用次序、合并方式决定了最终 loss 字典的 key 顺序（Python dict 保持插入序）。这一节回答三个问题：
284	
285	1. **谁先谁后？** 实例 → 语义 → 点提示 → 文本提示 → 对比。顺序本身不影响数值（都是加法），但影响日志里 key 的排列，也影响条件分支的写法。
286	2. **每一路拿到什么？** 关键差异是：`inst_criterion` 拿到的点提示参数是**原始的** `point_prompt_insts`（供其内部的蒸馏项使用），而不是重组过的 `point_prompt_gts`。
287	3. **最终字典长什么样？** 主配置下一次前向共 **10 个 loss key**，其中 3 个实例类 key 各自是「1 份主输出 + 6 层 aux 深监督」的累加，而不是像 DETR 那样每层一个带编号的 key。
288	
289	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
290	
291	```text
292	loss = inst_criterion(pred, inst_gts,
293	                      point_prompt_pred, point_prompt_insts)   # 原始提示 GT！
294	loss.update(sem_criterion(pred, sem_gts))                      # + seg_loss
295	if point_prompt_pred is not None:
296	    loss.update(point_prompt_inst_criterion(...))              # + point_prompt_inst_loss
297	if text_prompt_pred is not None:
298	    loss.update(text_prompt_inst_criterion(...))               # + text_prompt_inst_loss
299	loss.update(contrastive_criterion(pred, inst_gts,
300	              point_prompt_pred, point_prompt_gts,
301	              text_prompt_pred, text_prompt_gts))              # 恒调用
302	return loss
303	```
304

457	### 4.4 模块四：`seg_loss`——超点级交叉熵的三个细节
458	
459	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
460	
461	语义分割的监督目标：给每个**超点**（而非每个原始点）一个 20 类之一的标签，unlabeled 超点不参与。`ScanNetSemanticCriterion` 只用了 10 行核心代码，但有三个容易忽略的细节：
462	
463	1. **逐样本计算再平均**：交叉熵按场景各自算，再对批次求均值——不同场景超点数不同，若先拼接再算均值，大会被大场景主导（这里选择每个场景等权）。
464	2. **切掉预测的最后一列**：`sem_preds` 有 21 列（20 类 + unlabeled/背景列，来自球面分类的 back_token，u4-l4），训练时 `[:, :-1]` 丢掉第 21 列。
465	3. **`ignore_index=20` 忽略 unlabeled 超点**：GT 的 `argmax` 取值范围是 0~20，值为 20（unlabeled 兜底行胜出）的超点在交叉熵里被整体忽略——**与细节 2 是一对配合动作**。
466	
467	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
468	
469	```text
470	对批次中每个场景 i：
471	    pred_mask = sem_preds[i]                # (n_queries, 21)
472	    若 ignore_index >= 0:
473	        pred_mask = pred_mask[:, :-1]       # (n_queries, 20)：丢 unlabeled 列
474	    target = sem_gt.sp_masks.float().argmax(0)   # (n_queries,)，取值 0..20
475	    loss_i = F.cross_entropy(pred_mask, target, ignore_index=20)
476	                  # target==20 的位置（unlabeled 超点）被忽略
477	seg_loss = loss_weight × mean(loss_1..loss_B)
478	```
479	
480	为什么「切列 + ignore」要成对出现？交叉熵要求 `target` 的每个值要么在 `[0, C)` 内、要么等于 `ignore_index`。GT 里 unlabeled 超点的 `argmax` 是 20，而切掉最后一列后预测只有 20 类（下标 0~19）——如果没有 `ignore_index=20`，`F.cross_entropy` 会因越界标签直接报错；反过来，如果不切列而保留第 21 列，unlabeled 超点就会作为一个「真实类别」被学习，与「unlabeled 不参与监督」的意图相悖。两者配合的效果是：**unlabeled 超点对梯度零贡献，模型永远不会因为背景无标注而被惩罚**。
481	
482	顺带一提维度：`sem_preds` 的行是存活查询（`query_masks` 的列，见 4.2），所以这里的「超点级」确切说是「存活超点查询级」；推理时（u6-l1）语义预测再经 `superpoints` 索引映射回原始点。

484	#### 4.4.3 源码精读
485	
486	[uniseg3d/semantic_criterion.py:7-18](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/semantic_criterion.py#L7-L18)：注意它**不是** `nn.Module`，只是一个注册进 `MODELS` 的普通可调用对象，`__init__` 只存 `ignore_index` 与 `loss_weight` 两个数——没有可学习参数的损失完全不需要模块的开销。配置侧对应 [configs L70-73](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/configs/uniseg3d_1xb4_scannet_scanrefer_scannet200_unified.py#L70-L73)：`ignore_index=num_semantic_classes=20`、`loss_weight=0.2*sem_weight=0.2`。
487	
488	[uniseg3d/semantic_criterion.py:34-43](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/semantic_criterion.py#L34-L43) 是全部计算：L35 逐场景 zip `pred['sem_preds']` 与 GT；L36-37 当 `ignore_index >= 0` 时切掉预测最后一列；L38-41 用 `gt_mask.sp_masks.float().argmax(0)` 把 one-hot 语义行转回类别下标序列并做忽略式交叉熵；L42 对批次 `stack + mean` 后乘权重；L43 以 `dict(seg_loss=loss)` 返回——**返回 dict 是 mmengine 损失协议的硬性要求**，总调度靠 `update` 合并。
489	
490	它的输入 `sem_gts` 正是 4.1 里切出的后 21 行视图；`pred['sem_preds']` 来自解码器输出字典（[query_decoder.py:525-528](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/query_decoder.py#L525-L528) 的键之一），且只在最后一层解码器计算（u4-l4），所以语义路没有深监督。
491	
492	#### 4.4.4 代码实践
493	
494	**实践目标**：单独驱动 `ScanNetSemanticCriterion`，验证「unlabeled 超点零梯度」这一论断。
495	
496	**操作步骤**（示例代码，可存为 `uniseg3d-tutorial/playground_u5_l1_sem.py`）：
497	
498	```python
499	# 示例代码：验证 seg_loss 对 unlabeled 超点的忽略
500	import torch
501	import uniseg3d
502	from uniseg3d.semantic_criterion import ScanNetSemanticCriterion
503	from uniseg3d.structures import InstanceData_
504	
505	torch.manual_seed(0)
506	crit = ScanNetSemanticCriterion(ignore_index=20, loss_weight=0.2)
507	
508	n_q, n = 40, 20
509	sem_preds = [torch.randn(n_q, n + 1, requires_grad=True)]
510	
511	# 语义 GT：前 30 个查询有类别，后 10 个为 unlabeled（最后一行胜出）
512	gt = torch.zeros(n + 1, n_q, dtype=torch.bool)
513	ids = torch.randint(0, n, (30,))
514	gt[ids, torch.arange(30)] = True
515	gt[-1, 30:] = True
516	sem_gts = [InstanceData_(sp_masks=gt)]
517	
518	loss1 = crit(sem_preds, sem_gts)['seg_loss']
519	
520	# 把 unlabeled 查询（31..40 行）的预测 logits 改成完全不同的值
521	with torch.no_grad():
522	    sem_preds[0][30:] = torch.randn(10, n + 1) * 100
523	loss2 = crit(sem_preds, sem_gts)['seg_loss']
524	
525	print(f'loss1={loss1.item():.6f}  loss2={loss2.item():.6f}')
526	print('差值:', abs(loss1.item() - loss2.item()))
527	```
528	
529	**需要观察的现象**：尽管后 10 个查询（unlabeled）的预测被换成大相径庭的值，两次损失**完全相等**；再对 `loss1.backward()` 后检查 `sem_preds.grad`，后 10 行的梯度应全为 0。
530	
531	**预期结果**：差值为 0（浮点意义上相等），unlabeled 行梯度为 0。此行为可直接从 `ignore_index` 语义推出，具体数值待本地验证。
532	
533	#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案
534	
535	**练习 1**：`sem_preds` 有 21 列，为什么不直接用 21 列做交叉熵、把 unlabeled 当第 21 类学习？
536	
537	**答案**：unlabeled 不是语义概念上稳定的类别（ScanNet 的 `unlabeled` 是「无标注」的兜底，可能是任何东西），学它会逼模型给无标注区域编造一致性；两阶段做法（丢列 + 忽略）让这些超点完全不产生监督信号，背景列仅保留给推理时的「无对象」机制（u4-l4 的 back_token）。
538	
539	**练习 2**：`loss_weight=0.2` 相对实例类损失的内部权重（cls 0.5、BCE 1.0、dice 1.0）更小，这暗示什么？
540	
541	**答案**：这是多任务平衡的手段——语义任务每个超点都产生一份监督（监督密度高），实例任务只有 K+M 行掩码监督（密度低）；给语义损失更小的总权重，避免语义梯度在总损失中淹没实例梯度。具体比例是实验调参结果，读者可在 4.3.4 的脚本里改 `sem_weight` 观察各 key 相对量级（改配置需重新 build criterion）。
542	
543	**练习 3**：若某场景**所有**超点都是 unlabeled（`sp_masks` 只有最后一行为 True），`seg_loss` 会是多少？
544	
545	**答案**：`F.cross_entropy` 在所有位置都被忽略时的行为取决于 PyTorch 版本（对全忽略输入可能返回 0 或 `nan`）。真实 ScanNet 训练场景不会出现全 unlabeled 的情况；但自己构造极端假数据实验时若遇到 `nan`，应先检查 GT 是否全空（待本地验证）。
546	
547	---
548	
549	## 5. 综合实践
550	
551	**任务：做一次「损失字典体检」，把本讲四个模块串起来。**
552	
553	在 4.3.4 脚本的基础上完成下面三步：
554	
555	1. **体检一（拆分几何）**：把 `insts[0]` 构造里的 `K` 从 3 改成 6（总行数 29），不改其他任何东西，重新运行。观察 `inst_loss` 系列仍在（实例视图自动变成 8 行），`seg_loss` 不受影响——验证 4.1 的「一刀切」公式对任意 K、M 成立。
556	2. **体检二（query_masks）**：把 `keep = torch.randperm(n_sp)[:n_q]` 的 `n_q` 分别改成 30 和 40 各跑一次，观察 `seg_loss` 与 `inst_loss` 数值变化而所有 key 名不变——验证 4.2 的「列裁剪」只影响数值不影响结构；同时确认 `sem_preds` 等张量的形状要同步改（形状契约）。
557	3. **体检三（权重敏感性）**：用 `--cfg-options` 思路或直接改内存中的配置 dict（`cfg.model.criterion.sem_criterion.loss_weight = 1.0` 后再 `MODELS.build`），把 `seg_loss` 权重从 0.2 提到 1.0，观察打印中 `seg_loss` 数值精确变为原来的 5 倍、其余 key 不变——验证 4.4 的权重只在自己的分支内生效。
558	
559	最后把三次运行的关键输出（key 列表 + 每个数值）整理成一张对照表。如果本地已能跑真实训练（u1-l2），再抽一条真实日志的 `loss:` 行做第四列对照，键名应完全一致（数值不同是正常的——真实模型是训练中的网络而非随机数）。
560	
561	以上观察点均可从本讲源码分析直接推出，具体数值待本地验证。
562	
563	## 6. 本讲小结
564	
565	- `ScanNetUnifiedCriterion` 是**总调度**：`__init__` 用 `MODELS.build` 装配五个子损失，`__call__` 先把每份 GT 按 `[:-n-1]` / `[-n-1:]` 一刀切成实例视图（base 实例 + SAM3D 伪掩码）与语义视图（21 行 one-hot，末行 unlabeled 兜底），`labels_3d`、`is_novel` 与行切片同步。
566	- `query_masks` 是 `sp_masks` 的**列子集视图**：`_select_queries` 按 `query_thr=0.5` 随机丢查询时同步裁列，行（GT 条目）不变；语义路优先消费 `query_masks[-n-1:, :]`，实例路附带 `query_masks[:-n-1, :]`，保证 GT 与预测在同一套「存活查询」坐标上。
567	- 调用顺序固定为**实例 → 语义 → 点提示 → 文本提示 → 对比**，靠 `dict.update` 合并；`inst_criterion` 拿原始 `point_prompt_insts`（供蒸馏），两个提示 criterion 有判空保护而对比损失没有——它依赖训练管线恒产出两类提示这一约定。
568	- 主配置下一次前向共 **10 个 loss key**：`inst_loss`/`ov_inst_loss`/`iou_inst_loss`（各为 1+6 层深监督累加）、`IntrinsicPointAndQuery_loss`、`seg_loss`（仅末层 1 份）、`point_prompt_inst_loss`、`text_prompt_inst_loss`、`contrastive_loss`、`rank_loss`、`pseudo_ditribute_loss`（源码拼写）。
569	- `seg_loss` 是超点级交叉熵，三个细节：逐样本计算再批次平均；`[:, :-1]` 丢掉预测的 unlabeled 列；`ignore_index=20` 让 unlabeled 超点零梯度——切列与忽略必须成对，否则越界报错或学到伪背景类。
570	- `ScanNetSemanticCriterion` 不是 `nn.Module` 而是注册进 `MODELS` 的可调用对象，「损失=配置构建的可调用体、返回 dict」是 mmengine 的损失协议。
571	
572	## 7. 下一步学习建议
573	
574	本讲只看了各子损失的**接口与返回**，下一讲 u5-l2《匹配器 SparseMatcher 与代价函数》将钻进 `inst_criterion` 的第一站：`QueryClassificationCost`/`MaskBCECost`/`MaskDiceCost` 三种代价如何算、`SparseMatcher` 如何利用本讲传递的 `query_masks` 只在允许的 query-GT 组合里做 topk 稀疏匹配。建议在阅读前先自己重看 [unified_criterion.py:35-41](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/unified_criterion.py#L35-L41)（`query_masks` 如何随 `inst_gt` 下发）与 [instance_criterion.py:383-395](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/instance_criterion.py#L383-L395)（匹配器被调用的现场），并思考：超点查询天然携带归属信息时，为什么还需要一个匹配器？（答案在 u5-l2 揭晓：`is_novel` 拆出的 base 路仍需在「多个候选超点都部分覆盖同一实例」时选出最佳配对。）

# 损失总调度 ScanNetUnifiedCriterion 与语义损失

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. **看懂 `gt_sp_masks` 的行布局如何在损失侧被一刀切开**：前段（实例 + 伪掩码）喂给实例类损失，后 `n+1` 行（语义 one-hot，含 stuff 类与 unlabeled 兜底行）喂给语义损失，`labels_3d` 与 `is_novel` 同步行切。
2. **说清 `query_masks` 的来龙去脉**：它为什么是 `sp_masks` 的「列视图」，查询随机采样后为什么要同步切列，以及它在五个子损失之间如何传递。
3. **列出一次训练前向产生的全部 loss key**：共 10 个（`inst_loss`、`ov_inst_loss`、`iou_inst_loss`、`IntrinsicPointAndQuery_loss`、`seg_loss`、`point_prompt_inst_loss`、`text_prompt_inst_loss`、`contrastive_loss`、`rank_loss`、`pseudo_ditribute_loss`），并知道每个 key 由哪个子损失产出、带什么权重。
4. **逐行读懂 `ScanNetSemanticCriterion`** 的超点级交叉熵，特别是「切掉预测最后一列 + `ignore_index` 忽略 unlabeled」这一对配合动作。

本讲是第 5 单元（训练机制）的第一讲：我们只站在**总调度**的视角看「一份 GT 如何分发、一份 loss 字典如何合并」，各子损失内部的匹配与蒸馏机制留给后续讲义（u5-l2 ~ u5-l6）逐个拆解。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 交叉熵损失回顾

多分类交叉熵衡量预测分布与真实分布的差异。对单个样本，设预测 logits 经 softmax 得到概率 \( p = (p_0, p_1, \dots, p_{C-1}) \)，真实类别为 \( y \)，则：

\[
\mathcal{L}_{ce} = -\log p_y
\]

PyTorch 的 `F.cross_entropy(input, target)` 中，`input` 是形状 `(N, C)` 的 logits，`target` 是形状 `(N,)` 的类别下标。若某些位置的真实标签是「不可信/不参与训练」的（比如未标注点），可用 `ignore_index` 把它们排除在平均之外——这是本讲语义损失的关键机制。

### 2.2 本讲要继承的前几讲结论

| 来自 | 结论 | 本讲如何使用 |
|---|---|---|
| u3-l3 | `AddSuperPointAnnotations` 产出 `gt_sp_masks`：行 = [K 个 base 实例行 \| M 个 SAM3D 伪掩码行 \| 21 个语义行]，每列至多一个 True；`gt_labels_3d`、`is_novel` 与总行数同长 | 本讲的核心输入，损失侧按 `[:-n-1]` / `[-n-1:]` 切开 |
| u3-l2 / u4-l6 | `InstanceData_` 是放宽字段等长断言的实例容器 | 总调度用它重组各路 GT |
| u4-l1 | `loss()` 前向中 `_select_queries` 按 `query_thr=0.5` 随机保留 50%~100% 的超点查询（上限 3500） | 被丢弃的查询列需要从 GT 中同步裁掉，这就是 `query_masks` |
| u4-l3 / u4-l4 | 解码器迭代预测：主输出 + 6 层 `aux_outputs` 深监督；`sem_preds` 只在最后一层计算一次 | 解释为什么 `inst_loss` 是 7 份累加、`seg_loss` 只有 1 份 |
| u2-l1 / u2-l2 | 配置字符串经 `MODELS.build` 递归实例化；criterion 也是 model 配置的一个子树 | 五个子损失由总调度的 `__init__` 逐一 build |

### 2.3 「损失调度器」是什么

在 mmengine 体系里，损失不必是模型 `forward` 里的几行代码，也可以像搭积木一样做成**可调用对象**（callable）：`__init__` 里构建子损失，`__call__(pred, gt)` 里计算并返回一个 `{loss_name: tensor}` 字典。Runner 的训练循环拿到这个字典后，把所有 value 求和当作总损失反传，key 则原样打进训练日志。**所以「一次前向有哪些 loss key」是直接可以从日志里核对的事实**——这也是本讲实践任务的验收标准。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 模块一：`__call__` 中的 GT 拆分逻辑

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

UniSeg3D 的六类任务共用一次前向，但不同任务需要**不同形态的监督信号**：

- 实例类任务（全景/实例/开放词汇）需要「每个 GT 实例一条掩码行 + 类别标签」；
- 语义任务需要「每个超点属于哪个语义类」的逐列类别标签；
- 交互式/指代任务需要与提示一一对应的小份 GT。

而数据管线（u3-l3）只产出**一张**大布尔矩阵 `gt_sp_masks`（连同同长的 `gt_labels_3d`、`is_novel`）。于是总调度 `ScanNetUnifiedCriterion` 的第一职责就是**拆分发料**：把这张矩阵按行切开，重组出三份（或五份）GT 视图，分别交给对应子损失。

为什么不干脆在数据管线里直接产出多份 GT？因为行布局天然共享同一套超点列（`scatter_mean` 多数投票只算一次），拆分放到损失侧做，数据侧只需存一份，批处理与提示注入（u4-l6）也能统一操作。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

先回顾行布局（u3-l3 的结论，本讲直接使用）。设一个场景有 \( K \) 个 base 实例、\( M \) 个 SAM3D 伪掩码、\( n = 20 \) 个语义类、超点数为 \( S \)，则：

\[
\underbrace{\text{gt\_sp\_masks}}_{(K+M+n+1)\ \times\ S}
= \left[
\underbrace{I_1,\dots,I_K}_{\text{base 实例行}}\ ;\ 
\underbrace{P_1,\dots,P_M}_{\text{SAM3D 伪掩码行}}\ ;\ 
\underbrace{C_0,C_1,\dots,C_{19},U}_{\text{语义 one-hot 行（末行 } U \text{ 为 unlabeled 兜底）}}
\right]
\]

其中语义 21 行 = wall（id 0）+ floor（id 1）+ 18 个 things 类（id 2~19）+ unlabeled 兜底行。注意**实例部分不含 stuff 类**——u3-l3 里 wall/floor 与未标注点在进入 one-hot 前就被置 -1 剔除了。

总调度的拆分只依赖一个数字 \( n+1 = 21 \)（拆分点固定在倒数第 21 行）：

```text

对批次里每个场景 i：

    sem_gt.sp_masks  = query_masks[-21:, :]   （有 query_masks 时）
```

### 4.2 模块二：`query_masks`——查询采样后的 GT 同步裁剪

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`sp_masks` 的列坐标是「场景内全部超点」。但 u4-l1 讲过：训练前向里 `_select_queries` 会按 `query_thr=0.5` 随机丢弃一部分超点查询（省算力 + 增广效果），只有存活查询才进入解码器。于是产生一个对齐问题：**预测 `sem_preds`/`masks` 的第 j 列对应的是「存活查询 j」，而 GT 的第 c 列对应的是「超点 c」——两套列坐标不一致了**。

解法：采样时把被选中的超点下标 `ids` 记下来，用 `sp_masks[:, ids]` 把 GT 的列同步裁剪到存活查询上，结果存成 `query_masks`。所以：

- `sp_masks` = 完整视图：行 = GT 条目，列 = **全部超点**；
- `query_masks` = 训练视图：行 = GT 条目（**行不变**），列 = **存活的查询**。

`query_masks` 在总调度里被切片后随各路 GT 一起传给子损失；匹配器（u5-l2）据此只在存活查询上做匹配，损失计算也在存活列上进行——被丢弃的查询从训练中完全消失，等价于「这个超点今天不参与监督」。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
_select_queries（每个场景）：
    若 query_thr < 1：
        n ∼ Uniform(query_thr, 1) × 超点数，再截断到 ≤ 3500
        ids = 随机排列取前 n 个            # 存活超点的原始下标
        queries = 超点特征[ids]            # 预测侧：只保留这些查询
        query_masks = sp_masks[:, ids]     # GT 侧：列同步裁剪
    否则：
        queries = 全部超点特征
        query_masks = sp_masks             # 退化为完整视图
```

随后在总调度里：`sem_gt` 优先用 `query_masks[-n-1:, :]`，`inst_gt` 附带 `query_masks[:-n-1, :]`（见 4.1.3）；提示 GT 的 `query_masks` 原样透传（提示查询是从特定超点生成的，天然在存活集合内，无需再裁）。

### 4.3 模块三：五个子损失的调用顺序与 loss 字典合并

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

拆分完 GT，总调度开始「发货」。五个子损失的调用次序、合并方式决定了最终 loss 字典的 key 顺序（Python dict 保持插入序）。这一节回答三个问题：

1. **谁先谁后？** 实例 → 语义 → 点提示 → 文本提示 → 对比。顺序本身不影响数值（都是加法），但影响日志里 key 的排列，也影响条件分支的写法。
2. **每一路拿到什么？** 关键差异是：`inst_criterion` 拿到的点提示参数是**原始的** `point_prompt_insts`（供其内部的蒸馏项使用），而不是重组过的 `point_prompt_gts`。
3. **最终字典长什么样？** 主配置下一次前向共 **10 个 loss key**，其中 3 个实例类 key 各自是「1 份主输出 + 6 层 aux 深监督」的累加，而不是像 DETR 那样每层一个带编号的 key。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
loss = inst_criterion(pred, inst_gts,
                      point_prompt_pred, point_prompt_insts)   # 原始提示 GT！
loss.update(sem_criterion(pred, sem_gts))                      # + seg_loss
if point_prompt_pred is not None:
    loss.update(point_prompt_inst_criterion(...))              # + point_prompt_inst_loss
if text_prompt_pred is not None:
    loss.update(text_prompt_inst_criterion(...))               # + text_prompt_inst_loss
loss.update(contrastive_criterion(pred, inst_gts,
              point_prompt_pred, point_prompt_gts,
              text_prompt_pred, text_prompt_gts))              # 恒调用
return loss
```

注意两个不对称的设计：

- **两个提示 criterion 有 `is not None` 保护**（[L68](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/unified_criterion.py#L68)、[L71](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/unified_criterion.py#L71)），**对比损失没有**——[contrastive_criterion.py:50](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/contrastive_criterion.py#L50) 直接对 `point_prompt_pred['contras_embeds']` 下标，传 `None` 会抛 `TypeError`。它敢这么写，是因为训练管线里 `PointPromptGeneration` 与 `TextPromptGeneration` 恒执行（[config train_pipeline](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/configs/uniseg3d_1xb4_scannet_scanrefer_scannet200_unified.py#L172-L180)），两个提示键在训练批次中总是存在。**自己写假数据做实验时必须同时构造两路提示，否则走到 L74 就会崩**——这是本讲实践脚本设计的依据。
- **对比损失的内部保护靠「跳过」而非「判空」**：[contrastive_criterion.py:57-59](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/contrastive_criterion.py#L57-L59) 在某场景 `text_object_id` 为空时 `continue`；全部为空时返回 `contrastive_loss=0`（[L107-110](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/contrastive_criterion.py#L107-L110)）。

**练习 2**：把 `pred_iou` 改为 `False`（[config L13](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/configs/uniseg3d_1xb4_scannet_scanrefer_scannet200_unified.py#L13)），loss 字典会少哪些 key？

### 4.4 模块四：`seg_loss`——超点级交叉熵的三个细节

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

语义分割的监督目标：给每个**超点**（而非每个原始点）一个 20 类之一的标签，unlabeled 超点不参与。`ScanNetSemanticCriterion` 只用了 10 行核心代码，但有三个容易忽略的细节：

1. **逐样本计算再平均**：交叉熵按场景各自算，再对批次求均值——不同场景超点数不同，若先拼接再算均值，大会被大场景主导（这里选择每个场景等权）。
2. **切掉预测的最后一列**：`sem_preds` 有 21 列（20 类 + unlabeled/背景列，来自球面分类的 back_token，u4-l4），训练时 `[:, :-1]` 丢掉第 21 列。
3. **`ignore_index=20` 忽略 unlabeled 超点**：GT 的 `argmax` 取值范围是 0~20，值为 20（unlabeled 兜底行胜出）的超点在交叉熵里被整体忽略——**与细节 2 是一对配合动作**。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

```text
对批次中每个场景 i：
    pred_mask = sem_preds[i]                # (n_queries, 21)
    若 ignore_index >= 0:
        pred_mask = pred_mask[:, :-1]       # (n_queries, 20)：丢 unlabeled 列
    target = sem_gt.sp_masks.float().argmax(0)   # (n_queries,)，取值 0..20
    loss_i = F.cross_entropy(pred_mask, target, ignore_index=20)
                  # target==20 的位置（unlabeled 超点）被忽略
seg_loss = loss_weight × mean(loss_1..loss_B)
```

为什么「切列 + ignore」要成对出现？交叉熵要求 `target` 的每个值要么在 `[0, C)` 内、要么等于 `ignore_index`。GT 里 unlabeled 超点的 `argmax` 是 20，而切掉最后一列后预测只有 20 类（下标 0~19）——如果没有 `ignore_index=20`，`F.cross_entropy` 会因越界标签直接报错；反过来，如果不切列而保留第 21 列，unlabeled 超点就会作为一个「真实类别」被学习，与「unlabeled 不参与监督」的意图相悖。两者配合的效果是：**unlabeled 超点对梯度零贡献，模型永远不会因为背景无标注而被惩罚**。

顺带一提维度：`sem_preds` 的行是存活查询（`query_masks` 的列，见 4.2），所以这里的「超点级」确切说是「存活超点查询级」；推理时（u6-l1）语义预测再经 `superpoints` 索引映射回原始点。

#### 4.4.3 源码精读

[uniseg3d/semantic_criterion.py:7-18](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/semantic_criterion.py#L7-L18)：注意它**不是** `nn.Module`，只是一个注册进 `MODELS` 的普通可调用对象，`__init__` 只存 `ignore_index` 与 `loss_weight` 两个数——没有可学习参数的损失完全不需要模块的开销。配置侧对应 [configs L70-73](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/configs/uniseg3d_1xb4_scannet_scanrefer_scannet200_unified.py#L70-L73)：`ignore_index=num_semantic_classes=20`、`loss_weight=0.2*sem_weight=0.2`。

[uniseg3d/semantic_criterion.py:34-43](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/semantic_criterion.py#L34-L43) 是全部计算：L35 逐场景 zip `pred['sem_preds']` 与 GT；L36-37 当 `ignore_index >= 0` 时切掉预测最后一列；L38-41 用 `gt_mask.sp_masks.float().argmax(0)` 把 one-hot 语义行转回类别下标序列并做忽略式交叉熵；L42 对批次 `stack + mean` 后乘权重；L43 以 `dict(seg_loss=loss)` 返回——**返回 dict 是 mmengine 损失协议的硬性要求**，总调度靠 `update` 合并。

它的输入 `sem_gts` 正是 4.1 里切出的后 21 行视图；`pred['sem_preds']` 来自解码器输出字典（[query_decoder.py:525-528](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/query_decoder.py#L525-L528) 的键之一），且只在最后一层解码器计算（u4-l4），所以语义路没有深监督。

#### 4.4.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：单独驱动 `ScanNetSemanticCriterion`，验证「unlabeled 超点零梯度」这一论断。

**操作步骤**（示例代码，可存为 `uniseg3d-tutorial/playground_u5_l1_sem.py`）：

```python
# 示例代码：验证 seg_loss 对 unlabeled 超点的忽略
import torch
import uniseg3d
from uniseg3d.semantic_criterion import ScanNetSemanticCriterion
from uniseg3d.structures import InstanceData_

torch.manual_seed(0)
crit = ScanNetSemanticCriterion(ignore_index=20, loss_weight=0.2)

n_q, n = 40, 20
sem_preds = [torch.randn(n_q, n + 1, requires_grad=True)]

# 语义 GT：前 30 个查询有类别，后 10 个为 unlabeled（最后一行胜出）
gt = torch.zeros(n + 1, n_q, dtype=torch.bool)
ids = torch.randint(0, n, (30,))
gt[ids, torch.arange(30)] = True
gt[-1, 30:] = True
sem_gts = [InstanceData_(sp_masks=gt)]

loss1 = crit(sem_preds, sem_gts)['seg_loss']

# 把 unlabeled 查询（31..40 行）的预测 logits 改成完全不同的值
with torch.no_grad():
    sem_preds[0][30:] = torch.randn(10, n + 1) * 100
loss2 = crit(sem_preds, sem_gts)['seg_loss']

print(f'loss1={loss1.item():.6f}  loss2={loss2.item():.6f}')
print('差值:', abs(loss1.item() - loss2.item()))
```

**需要观察的现象**：尽管后 10 个查询（unlabeled）的预测被换成大相径庭的值，两次损失**完全相等**；再对 `loss1.backward()` 后检查 `sem_preds.grad`，后 10 行的梯度应全为 0。

**预期结果**：差值为 0（浮点意义上相等），unlabeled 行梯度为 0。此行为可直接从 `ignore_index` 语义推出，具体数值待本地验证。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`sem_preds` 有 21 列，为什么不直接用 21 列做交叉熵、把 unlabeled 当第 21 类学习？

**答案**：unlabeled 不是语义概念上稳定的类别（ScanNet 的 `unlabeled` 是「无标注」的兜底，可能是任何东西），学它会逼模型给无标注区域编造一致性；两阶段做法（丢列 + 忽略）让这些超点完全不产生监督信号，背景列仅保留给推理时的「无对象」机制（u4-l4 的 back_token）。

**练习 2**：`loss_weight=0.2` 相对实例类损失的内部权重（cls 0.5、BCE 1.0、dice 1.0）更小，这暗示什么？

**答案**：这是多任务平衡的手段——语义任务每个超点都产生一份监督（监督密度高），实例任务只有 K+M 行掩码监督（密度低）；给语义损失更小的总权重，避免语义梯度在总损失中淹没实例梯度。具体比例是实验调参结果，读者可在 4.3.4 的脚本里改 `sem_weight` 观察各 key 相对量级（改配置需重新 build criterion）。

**练习 3**：若某场景**所有**超点都是 unlabeled（`sp_masks` 只有最后一行为 True），`seg_loss` 会是多少？

**答案**：`F.cross_entropy` 在所有位置都被忽略时的行为取决于 PyTorch 版本（对全忽略输入可能返回 0 或 `nan`）。真实 ScanNet 训练场景不会出现全 unlabeled 的情况；但自己构造极端假数据实验时若遇到 `nan`，应先检查 GT 是否全空（待本地验证）。

**任务：做一次「损失字典体检」，把本讲四个模块串起来。**

2. **体检二（query_masks）**：把 `keep = torch.randperm(n_sp)[:n_q]` 的 `n_q` 分别改成 30 和 40 各跑一次，观察 `seg_loss` 与 `inst_loss` 数值变化而所有 key 名不变——验证 4.2 的「列裁剪」只影响数值不影响结构；同时确认 `sem_preds` 等张量的形状要同步改（形状契约）。
3. **体检三（权重敏感性）**：用 `--cfg-options` 思路或直接改内存中的配置 dict（`cfg.model.criterion.sem_criterion.loss_weight = 1.0` 后再 `MODELS.build`），把 `seg_loss` 权重从 0.2 提到 1.0，观察打印中 `seg_loss` 数值精确变为原来的 5 倍、其余 key 不变——验证 4.4 的权重只在自己的分支内生效。

最后把三次运行的关键输出（key 列表 + 每个数值）整理成一张对照表。如果本地已能跑真实训练（u1-l2），再抽一条真实日志的 `loss:` 行做第四列对照，键名应完全一致（数值不同是正常的——真实模型是训练中的网络而非随机数）。

以上观察点均可从本讲源码分析直接推出，具体数值待本地验证。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `ScanNetUnifiedCriterion` 是**总调度**：`__init__` 用 `MODELS.build` 装配五个子损失，`__call__` 先把每份 GT 按 `[:-n-1]` / `[-n-1:]` 一刀切成实例视图（base 实例 + SAM3D 伪掩码）与语义视图（21 行 one-hot，末行 unlabeled 兜底），`labels_3d`、`is_novel` 与行切片同步。
- `query_masks` 是 `sp_masks` 的**列子集视图**：`_select_queries` 按 `query_thr=0.5` 随机丢查询时同步裁列，行（GT 条目）不变；语义路优先消费 `query_masks[-n-1:, :]`，实例路附带 `query_masks[:-n-1, :]`，保证 GT 与预测在同一套「存活查询」坐标上。
- 调用顺序固定为**实例 → 语义 → 点提示 → 文本提示 → 对比**，靠 `dict.update` 合并；`inst_criterion` 拿原始 `point_prompt_insts`（供蒸馏），两个提示 criterion 有判空保护而对比损失没有——它依赖训练管线恒产出两类提示这一约定。
- 主配置下一次前向共 **10 个 loss key**：`inst_loss`/`ov_inst_loss`/`iou_inst_loss`（各为 1+6 层深监督累加）、`IntrinsicPointAndQuery_loss`、`seg_loss`（仅末层 1 份）、`point_prompt_inst_loss`、`text_prompt_inst_loss`、`contrastive_loss`、`rank_loss`、`pseudo_ditribute_loss`（源码拼写）。
- `seg_loss` 是超点级交叉熵，三个细节：逐样本计算再批次平均；`[:, :-1]` 丢掉预测的 unlabeled 列；`ignore_index=20` 让 unlabeled 超点零梯度——切列与忽略必须成对，否则越界报错或学到伪背景类。
- `ScanNetSemanticCriterion` 不是 `nn.Module` 而是注册进 `MODELS` 的可调用对象，「损失=配置构建的可调用体、返回 dict」是 mmengine 的损失协议。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

本讲只看了各子损失的**接口与返回**，下一讲 u5-l2《匹配器 SparseMatcher 与代价函数》将钻进 `inst_criterion` 的第一站：`QueryClassificationCost`/`MaskBCECost`/`MaskDiceCost` 三种代价如何算、`SparseMatcher` 如何利用本讲传递的 `query_masks` 只在允许的 query-GT 组合里做 topk 稀疏匹配。建议在阅读前先自己重看 [unified_criterion.py:35-41](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/unified_criterion.py#L35-L41)（`query_masks` 如何随 `inst_gt` 下发）与 [instance_criterion.py:383-395](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/instance_criterion.py#L383-L395)（匹配器被调用的现场），并思考：超点查询天然携带归属信息时，为什么还需要一个匹配器？（答案在 u5-l2 揭晓：`is_novel` 拆出的 base 路仍需在「多个候选超点都部分覆盖同一实例」时选出最佳配对。）

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
